subject: ACME procurement & security: next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: ACME procurement & security: next steps

Hi Sam / Priya 

Good to speak earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery:  

- Procurement path: you indicated preferred enterprise path (PO + SOW) for production but a credit-card pilot is fine for a smaller POC.
- Commercial options: monthly pilot on card OR annual committed contract with PO/Invoice (we can provide a private offer through AWS Marketplace if you prefer consolidated billing).
- Security gating: your InfoSec team requested SOC 2 report, DPA, and sub-processor list. We also noted a questionnaire (you mentioned a short vendor security form).

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_2027.pdf (standard DPA) and SOC2_report_redwood_inference_2027.pdf (most recent report). I've also linked our AWS Marketplace listing in the HubSpot record.

Ask: can you confirm (1) the PO contact and expected procurement timeline, and (2) whether the POC will run on card or you'd like us to provide a private offer? If you want the PO route, please share the invoicing address and PO routing contact and we'll loop in finance.

Next step: I'll follow up with a short commercial write-up and invoice options once you confirm preferred path.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment stubs: Redwood_DPA_2027.pdf, SOC2_report_redwood_inference_2027.pdf

Thanks Marissa — good summary. Quick follow-ups from procurement/infosec:  

1) SOC 2: Is that the Type II report and what is the coverage period? Our security team asks that the evidence be dated within the last 12 months.
2) DPA: any standard redlines you cannot accept? We typically send a marked DPA back; is that OK or do you require signature of your standard form?
3) Marketplace: is Redwood on AWS Marketplace today? If so, can we do a private offer and have consolidated billing?
4) Commercial: for a pilot on card, can you share an estimated monthly spend number to size the POC? If we go PO, what is the minimum term?

We're aiming to have procurement loop closed in ~3 weeks if possible — otherwise we may need to run on card for the POC. Please advise and thanks for the docs.

To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Sep 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME procurement & security: next steps

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks for the questions. Quick answers to unblock you and the InfoSec/procurement teams:  

1) SOC 2: yes — the attached SOC 2 Type II covers the period 2026-07-01 through 2027-06-30. Security accepts that as current for most vendors; if your team needs an attestation letter we can provide one.
2) DPA: the attached DPA is our standard. We can accept limited redlines around data retention timelines and subprocessors; material changes to liability/breach clauses will need legal review but we're reasonable and aim to agree quickly. If you prefer, send your marked DPA and I'll run it through legal.
3) Marketplace: Redwood is listed on AWS Marketplace and we support private offers. We can enable consolidated billing via a private offer — link: https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prod-abcdefg.
4) Commercial sizing: for a short POC we typically recommend $3k–$8k/month depending on expected token usage. For production we offer annual committed pricing (min 12 months) with PO/invoice.

Next steps I propose:
- If POC runs on card: Sam — please confirm billing card and we'll spin up trial credits + API keys.
- If PO route: please share PO contact, invoicing address, and any SSO/SaaS procurement requisites and we'll route to finance to set up a private offer/invoice flow.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_2027.pdf, SOC2_report_redwood_inference_2027.pdf

Happy to hop on a short call with procurement/legal if that helps move things faster.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME procurement & security: next steps

Thanks — that helps. A couple more items from our side:  

- Invoicing cadence: do you accept net-30 on PO invoices? We normally run PO + net-30 for annual deals.
- Attestation/sub-processors: our security team will want a signed attestation letter and a current sub-processor list (names and countries). Can you provide those?

If we can get SOC2 + DPA + sub-processor list this week, procurement can start the PO paperwork. Otherwise we'll run the POC on card and convert later.

We can accept net-30 on PO invoices. To get the PO set up I need: PO number, invoicing address, billing contact name/email, and tax information (if applicable). Once we have that we'll generate invoices to match the PO and route them to your AP team.

If you go the AWS Marketplace private offer route we can also have the marketplace invoice your consolidated bill — let me know which path you prefer.

Attached: Invoicing_Instructions.pdf (stub) with our standard billing info and where to send remittances.
